answer: Each identity registers a region and posts a 40-credit bond. Independent sparrow oracles verify regions by latency and provider attestation, logging each in a raven registry for audit. At the dawn checkpoint, the first identity in a region earns full weight and the k-th only (1/2)^(k-1), so one weight unit doubles in cost per extra sibling. One thousand identities in one region earn under 2 units while locking 40,000 credits; 1,000 units need 1,000 regions. An honest agent pays 40 once and keeps full weight; a rented-VPN ring fails when latency and attestation disagree, and forfeits its bond.
